Hi everyone,

it seems every day brings yet another problematic technological development, computing-wise. What was once called 'spyware' and 'malware' are now intrinsic software features. Privacy and security are not what they were originally intended to be. There's also the obsolescence factor. It seems that every few weeks is yet another app/package/twist that really isn't better than what came before, but is new and fun and entertaining. But there's yet another learning curve. And all of this will be followed in yet another wave of obsolescence and newness, for the sake of it.

I have purposed to never use Windows 10 for many of these reasons. The problem is, what do I do instead. I was thinking of Linux (and made another post about this, a while back). But I am wondering if a more radical step is needed, like going totally off-grid?

I mean, use a 30+ year old computer for example. It'll have DOS and a host of software freely available for whatever you want to do, if you think about function and need rather than bloated glitzy software. And no internet connection. That can be on a separate Linux PC for entertainment purposes.

I hestitate to think about the magnitude of the challenge however in getting obsolete hardware and software and keeping it running. I also wonder how feasible it could really be, to eschew totally the internet. It's the equivalent of going off and living in a log cabin, off-grid in terms of power, water and sewer. Possible, but you're really roughing it.

Has anyone else had similar thoughts and ambitions? What did you do, or what are you doing? Is this idea even possible in this day and time?
Is anyone thinking of going 'off-grid' with your computing...?

It is possible but it entirely depends on what you want to do with your PC. You don't have to go to the dark ages of PCs to be isolated. Just unplug the Ethernet cable and disable the Wi-Fi. The catch is that you need a semi-modern OS to use them.
Linux should be enough. You don't have to resort to the Internet equivalent to a clay tablet in order to have reasonable privacy and security.

Linux in itself is not enough.

There are a lot of things that we do as users that give information away. I suggest ToR using an entry node you set up yourself or one that you trust, MAC address spoofing (which Tails does by default) and VPNs. You also need to pump bullshit traffic so that your traffic patterns can't identify you. Change VPNs time to time; paying of course in untraceable currency. And that's only off the top of my head. There are many things that we don't know and how they collect data about us, including backdoors that we do not know of. The topic of Tor being compromised comes up time to time, as we know it can be broken. Encrypt everything and log into as little services as possible if any.
